Leadership Profile

Summary

The ten leadership actions taken from the role description (Define, Assess, Align, Delegate, Oversee, Authorize, Mentor, Hire, Report, Evangelize) and the evidence behind each: weekly-report entries, deliverables, risks, sessions led, meeting hours and colleague reviews. Every other page in this report carries the same actions as chips.

Key insights

Ten actions describe how this work was led: Define, Assess, Align, Delegate, Oversee, Authorize, Mentor, Hire, Report, Evangelize.

They come from the role and responsibilities document (supervisory role). Every weekly entry, deliverable, risk, session and meeting in this report carries up to three of them. 263 of the 371 weekly entries show at least one action, 177 of them in my own contribution text. 794 of 921 meeting hours carry an action; the rest are learning, company events and untitled meetings. The tags describe the type of action, not how well it was performed.

Deliver the committed 2026 AI compliance platform milestone on time for the agreed end-to-end workflow and release scope, while improving delivery readiness through AI-enabled traceability and stronger execution confidence.

G1.1Deliver the committed 2026 milestone on time, with BU/customer release acceptance and confirmation to adopt
G1.2Demonstrate by year-end that the AI-enabled traceability approach was used to support milestone delivery and reduce late traceability gaps versus the starting point.

AI traceability platform is deployed in five business contexts and scored an NPS of 10 from two customers. AI defect-triage assistant, an AI compliance platform Cohort 5 project still in delivery: by 16 November, its KPI dashboard recorded 2,890 successful events and 12,171 agent runs, and estimated 502.03 hours saved.

What came of it
  • AI traceability platform is now deployed in a business unit, a business unit, a business unit, SRC and a business unit. In a business unit the team deployed it with APIs integrated for AI features, and rolling it out to a business unit stakeholders as a pilot is the next step.
  • On a business unit thread an AI upskilling programme colleague wrote “Fantastic, thank you for confirming! And great work.” and asked for the AI traceability platform impacts to be added to the AI upskilling programme impact tracker and signed off, and the engineering group leadership thanked everyone for the successful deployment.
  • Two business customers each gave the AI compliance platform AI-powered V&V compliance work, which is AI traceability platform, an NPS of 10: the EI Image Informatics a business unit business on 29 May and a business unit on 2 June.
  • The Golden Thread Traceability milestone was delivered in week 4, and the milestone review confirmed the project stayed on track for its other milestones.
  • Questions raised in review made traceability-data gaps visible before incorrect mappings were built into the solution, and the ingestion process surfaced gaps in the business data that were being addressed.
  • Before deployment, teams beyond the original delivery took steps with AI traceability platform: an AI orchestration programme chose traceability as its first use case, a business unit set up AI traceability platform in its own AWS account, Ultrasound R&D worked through a setup path for a separate evaluation, and the Dhruv project asked to use it to review a UTS document.
  • Leaders asked for the work: one leader asked to share the AI traceability platform work with the VPC team, and I&D leadership-team members asked for the deck and for access.
  • The Inside AI compliance platform Special Edition spotlighted AI-powered end-to-end traceability for software verification and validation; its author puts the audience at more than 400 attendees.

The defect-triage project was funded as a six-month engagement, and by 16 November its KPI dashboard recorded 2,890 successful events and 12,171 agent runs, and estimated 502.03 hours saved.

What came of it
  • The Ultrasound defect-triage project moved from proposal to a funded, scoped six-month engagement in week 18, with business-owned requirements and milestone governance agreed.
  • AI defect-triage assistant entered delivery in week 23. Milestone 1 was completed across three sprints and 26 working days, with architecture sign-off, an end-to-end proof of concept on real data, and clearance to proceed to Milestone 2.
  • By 16 November, the AI defect-triage assistant KPI dashboard recorded 2,890 successful events (dashboard solution) and 12,171 runs of the AI-Triage Agent, and estimated 502.03 hours saved.
  • Milestone 2.1 was completed in week 39, with Azure DevOps story-creation integration, wider accuracy evaluation, and AI accuracy-feedback tracking added.
  • A project colleague reported that the combined tools triaged 1,300 failed test records in minutes instead of hours.
  • I set up a reusable KPI and value-measurement framework covering triage volume, automation coverage, labor-hour reduction, defect-identification latency, cycle time and adoption.
  • Another business group asked for an applicability review of the defect-triage capability.
  • I taught 20 colleagues to build agents with GitHub Copilot, rated 9.3 out of 10.

AI upskilling programme activities scored NPS 10, 10 and 9, and participants rated 7 of 15 sessions 9 out of 10 or higher.

  • I led 16 AI upskilling programme sessions between 26 March and 12 November, reaching 854 participants in the register.

  • AI upskilling programme activities I ran or set up scored an NPS of 10 from the North America Analytics community (an AI learning series that reached 267 employees at 9.44 out of 10 satisfaction, surveyed in Medallia), 10 from a business unit for the AI requirements checker deployment, and 9 from a business unit for AI skills at scale.
  • a business unit AI upskilling programme activity received an NPS of 9, and the sponsor recognized my role in setting up the engagement with a business unit.
  • The AI upskilling programme impact slide, which thanks me by name, reports 13 of 14 BUs engaged, 11 BUs adopting the Business Case AI Agent, and up to 50% shorter development cycle in one pilot. These are program-level figures.
  • Participants of the AI upskilling programme session on building practical agents thanked me in the chat.
  • The AI traceability platform impacts are being added to the AI upskilling programme impact tracker for sign-off (4 Nov).

SRC asked for a follow-up on the DORA wireframe, program nominations followed, and the DORA session was rated 9 out of 10.

What came of it
  • I created the DORA dashboard wireframe, described as a strong starting point (week 3), and shared it with SRC with team and program views and a proposed single the engineering group KPI (week 5).
  • SRC asked for a follow-up discussion on the wireframe, to understand what installation would mean for its environment (week 5).
  • Leadership asked which 2026 programs would set DORA improvement targets and track them to closure, and program nominations followed (weeks 8 and 9).
  • I consolidated the DORA program information into a single workbook (week 11).
  • A leader said they liked the wireframe. Another colleague built on the dashboard for their team, adding detail on software delivery and quality, and wrote that the summary for PMs and executives was one they loved.
  • I demonstrated the wireframe repository to participants of the DORA sessions, and passed it to a colleague, who used the concept to enhance his own DORA dashboard.
  • I taught DORA to 27 colleagues, rated 9.0 out of 10.
  • My prior-context evidence on the existing repository and hosted implementation helped the Software Excellence team judge overlap and reuse, supporting a shared scalable direction rather than parallel implementations (weeks 39 and 40).

Expert validation stopped unreliable check results from being treated as validated, and Patient Safety and Quality leadership featured requirements-review programme to 29,101 colleagues.

What came of it
  • For the product quality review Design Checklist automation, I produced the standards-basis documents and an updated assessment report for internal testing and reran the solution (week 39); the feasibility package had explicit evidence, standards interpretations and decision logic. I am a named co-author of the feasibility report, completed and circulated for a decision (week 42).
  • The updated tool output I supplied went through expert validation, which set out correction areas and prevented unreliable check results from being treated as validated conclusions (weeks 37 and 38).
  • Across a business unit, Ultrasound VM13 and a business unit Allegro, SMEs and the project lead validated a reduction from about two months to two weeks for the deep-dive assessment and remediation, using AI requirements checker, AI traceability platform and AI assessment tool.
  • Patient Safety and Quality leadership featured requirements-review programme in a post seen by 29,101 colleagues, and my own requirements-review programme testimonial post drew 10 comments.
  • The PS&Q Regions AI community invited me to speak on AI validation, a colleague asked to keep the recording of my requirements session, and another colleague asked for my help with a requirements-review programme project.

AI traceability platform

Leadership actions in this project
5businessesAI traceability platform deployed in a business unit, a business unit, a business unit, SRC and a business unit
Recorded
10 / 10NPSfrom a business unit and from a business unit
Recorded
4capabilitiesreleased in 9 weeks: traceability, impact assessment, test gaps, chatbot
Recorded
12 → 2weeksto prepare a compliance submission
Estimate

What it is

The problem

Release and submission readiness is slowed by fragmented DHF execution. Requirements, risks, tests and design evidence are disconnected, so traceability reconstruction, impact assessment and 510(k) submission evidence stay manual and prone to gaps.

The approach

Ingest and normalize DHF artifacts (requirements from ALMs, test cases and results, release documents), model the relationships in a graph database aligned to the V-model, visualize traceability, impact and requirements-to-test gaps, add AI for gap remediation and natural-language query, with human approval preserved.

Why it matters

AI traceability platform is an AI-powered V&V compliance platform that links design-history evidence in a graph database to give traceability, change-impact analysis and test-gap detection for medical device software.

What happened

Golden Thread Traceability (the traceability tool)

Ingests release documents from the businesses and shows end-to-end links (need, requirement, design, risk, test, result) as a graph, upstream and downstream.

Impact Assessment (impact analysis)

Shows which requirements, tests and other artifacts are affected when a requirement changes, with severity and a reason why each node appears.

Test scenario gap detection and generation

Finds requirements without test coverage and uses generative AI to propose test scenarios. First iteration only; live for a business unit first, SRC and a business unit planned after data validation.

2D/3D graph exploration, search, orphan-node view and export

Interactive 2D and 3D graph with node-type filtering, property search, orphaned-node detection and CSV/JSON export of traceability.

Gremlin query support and Graph Builder

Advanced users can run Gremlin graph queries; the Graph Builder auto-constructs Gremlin queries.

Semantic-search chatbot (natural-language query)

Users ask questions in natural language and get answers based on their ingested data. Described as the final feature planned under the AI compliance platform project; accuracy still being refined.

Automated ingestion pipeline

Automated project creation and infrastructure provisioning plus ingestion and gap identification from business documents; completed for SRC, a business unit and a business unit.

Self-hosted inner-source platform on AWS (Neptune graph)

Runs in business-managed AWS accounts on a Neptune graph database; inner sourced so any team can extend it.

Developer Portal access (no GitHub credentials)

Live the traceability tool data on the internal developer portal so anyone in the organization can open it without GitHub credentials. Staging first; production migration still a next step in Wk 9.
15 more

Windchill integration (direct read of DHF documents)

Retrieve controlled documents from Windchill instead of manual upload. Read APIs available and functional account in place; end-to-end flow was redirected to staging for testing.

Windchill MCP access

Agent-oriented access to Windchill through MCP is the preferred long-term interface; read-only API is the nearer path and write use cases are not defined.

AI traceability platform-native test-case generation engine for a business unit (BDD, RAG)

Proposed Cohort 5 extension to generate BDD test cases from URS/PRS/SRS and regenerate impacted tests. Did not advance in Cohort 5 selection.

Q&R compliance checks (policy rulebook / compliance monitoring)

Executable checks of standards (IEC 62304, ISO 13485). A Cohort 5 proposal of about an undisclosed amount, not started in Wk 9, and a speaker-note vision.

Living knowledge graph of engineering artifacts (AI Accelerator PoC)

Natural-language-queryable knowledge graph on top of existing ALM systems, funded as an the engineering group AI Accelerator proof of concept; conditional on a joint roadmap with Systems Engineering Excellence.

Deployment: a business unit

Release documents ingested into a Neptune graph (4150 nodes, 3150 edges in the 27 Jan snapshot). At Workshop 3, a business unit said priorities and budget prevented immediate handover and asked whether the environment could be paused or archived.
Data ingested (3 original lead businesses); handover paused at Wk 13

Deployment: SRC (a business unit)

1420 nodes and 2360 edges in the 27 Jan snapshot. At Workshop 3 SRC lacked the required a business unit AWS account and asked for cost; the reply was about an undisclosed amount per month for one business cluster. NPS of 10 reported 2 June 2026.
Data ingested; NPS 10; AWS account and cost query open at Wk 13

Deployment: a business unit (EI-CI-AV&I / EI-II a business unit)

3927 nodes and 8800 edges in the 27 Jan snapshot. Test-scenario generation went live for a business unit first. At Workshop 3 a business unit cited limited capacity and said the project needed to pause for now. Cohort 5 test-generation extension did not advance.
Data ingested; first to receive test-scenario generation; asked to pause at Wk 13; NPS 10

Deployment: a business unit

Not an original AI compliance platform sponsor. POC scope was IntraSight URS, PRS, ERS and test cases; first staging ingestion in Wk 16; app setup in a business unit AWS reported complete in Wk 21. Leadership Q&A cites a business unit with a December 2026 go-live.
Environment set up in a business unit AWS; business evaluation; go-live expected December 2026

Deployment: a business unit

Next step is a pilot with a business unit stakeholders. Impacts to be added to the AI upskilling programme tracker.
Deployed in a business unit's own AWS environment; rollout to stakeholders pending

Deployment: an AI orchestration programme (pilot)

Requested as a no-cost POC after the the engineering group roadshow, starting with traceability on a release artifact set. Access to S3, Lambda, ECR and Neptune hit setup challenges and the teams were asked to pause on 3 April; later follow-up still showed access open.
Paused

Deployment: Ultrasound R&D

An Ultrasound team with over 13,000 requirements asked about verifying only new, changed or impacted ones; Impact Assessment was positioned. A benefit-risk PoC was framed as an AI compliance platform extension. In Wk 32 a live demo and DOORS connectivity talk were offered.

Deployment: MR

MR appears in the Software Excellence portfolio that includes AI traceability platform, and as a business identified for cross-learning follow-up calls in the AI defect-triage assistant tracker.
